editorial:
Imagine being fourteen years old and suddenly feeling like the only adult in the room. That is exactly where you find yourself with Joe, a kid growing up in 1960s Montana. His dad, Jerry, is a golf pro who loses his job and hits a mid-life crisis, deciding to leave his family to fight forest fires up north. This leaves Joe and his mom, Jeanette, alone in a quiet town. You can really feel the tension as the family falls apart. It is not a loud movie with big explosions, but it captures that awkward and scary feeling of realizing your parents are just flawed people who do not have everything figured out.

The acting is what really makes this work, especially the way the kid plays Joe as he watches his mom struggle. It is a slow burn, so if you like fast action, this might feel too quiet for you. However, the scenery is beautiful and the emotions feel real. If you want to see it in the best quality, you should grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection or rent it on Apple TV to see all those Montana landscapes in crisp detail. It is a great pick for a quiet Sunday night when you want a story that actually makes you think about your own family.
endingExplained: The movie ends with Joe realizing his parents cannot save each other. After his dad comes home and tries to act like everything is fine, Joe sees the cracks in their marriage. He eventually leaves home to find his own path. The final scenes show him growing up and moving on, accepting that his childhood home was a place of instability. It wraps up by showing that Joe is the only one who truly matured during the crisis.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic family stories and character studies.
